label: The CRAFTING screen, across genres — recipe lists, ingredient rows read against inventory, quantity and craft-all, timed queues, station tiers, and upgrade trees with prerequisites
provenance: Web research on 2026-09-20, not owner screenshots. Eight community wikis of SHIPPED Roblox experiences were read as wikitext through each wiki's api.php endpoint (Fandom serves article HTML behind Cloudflare; api.php is open), and five DevForum topics were read through Discourse's own JSON endpoint at /t/<id>.json. No image, no Luau source and no asset is copied here. Each row records the exact URL it was read from, how it was fetched and on what date, so the claim can be re-checked. What is recorded is CONSTRUCTION — what is on the screen, how it is arranged, what states it has, what it does when a recipe is unaffordable or a queue is interrupted — not lore, stats or strategy. Where a claim is the wiki's own structure rather than the game's, that is said in the row.

references.source: https://fisch.fandom.com/wiki/Craftable_Rods — read on 2026-09-20 through https://fisch.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Craftable%20Rods&prop=wikitext&format=json, because Fandom serves its article HTML behind Cloudflare while api.php is open. Fisch is a shipped Roblox fishing game; the page documents the Crafting Altar in the Ancient Archives.
demonstrates: A RECIPE HAS THREE INDEPENDENT REQUIREMENT AXES AND TWO OF THEM CAN BE ZERO: a level gate, a currency price, and a material list. The page renders them as three fixed headings — 'Requirements' carrying Level and Price, then 'Needed Materials'. The Vineweaver Rod is Level 0 and 150,000 C$; the Rod of the Eternal King is Level 400 and 0 C$. THE MATERIAL LIST IS NEVER EMPTY: every rod tabbed on this page carries at least one ingredient, so the 'each can be zero' this row claimed until 2026-09-20 is false of the third axis. A requirement block that only renders the axes in play still changes shape between two rows of the same list, on the two axes that do reach zero.

AN INGREDIENT SLOT IS AN ITEM PLUS ITS VARIANT, NOT AN ITEM ID. Rod recipes on this page call for Mythical, Lunar, Frozen, Atlantean, Poisoned and Vined Driftwood as SIX different ingredients, and for Spirit Sea Mine and Spirit Speed Core. The page's ingredient index lists nine Driftwood rows in all — plain Driftwood plus eight mutations — of which Festive and Shrouded appear in no rod recipe here; the Shrouded variant that a recipe does call for is a Golden Sea Pearl. The crafting screen's match against inventory has to compare the modifier as well as the base item, and the ingredient chip has to show which variant.

AN INGREDIENT CAN BE UNOBTAINABLE BY GATHERING. The Evil Pitchfork needs one Evil Sigil, and the page's sub-bullet under that ingredient is 'Completing Crimson King's quest'. So the 'how do I get this' affordance on an ingredient chip is sometimes a quest, not a location.

THE WHOLE STATION IS GATED BEHIND A WORLD ACTION, NOT A LEVEL: the Notes say the player must have completed the Ancient Isle puzzle with the totems to access the area at all. The recipe-level gates are a second, finer gate inside a screen that some players cannot reach.

THE STRONGEST ROW IN THIS FILE'S INVENTORY-COUPLING: the page's own Notes warn 'Make sure to unfavorite the materials before crafting. Otherwise, it will appear as the player doesn't own the materials.' A protection flag set in the INVENTORY screen silently changes the CRAFTING screen's availability readout — the recipe reports the ingredient as missing rather than as protected. The two screens share one item list and disagree about it.

Quantities are written on both sides of the item in the same list — '1x Magic Thread' on some rows and 'Lunar Thread ×3' on others — which is what an ingredient line looks like when nobody owns the format.

references.source: https://robloxislands.fandom.com/wiki/Workbench and the four tier pages — read on 2026-09-20 through https://robloxislands.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Workbench&prop=wikitext&format=json and the same call for Workbench%20Tier%201, Workbench%20Tier%202, Workbench%20Tier%203 and Workbench%20Tier%204. Islands is a shipped Roblox sandbox; the workbench is its primary crafting station.
demonstrates: THE STATION'S OWN UPGRADE IS A ROW IN ITS OWN RECIPE LIST. The starter workbench has exactly two recipes: Wooden Pickaxe, and Workbench Tier 1 for 5 Oak Wood and 2 Iron Ore. The upgrade is not a separate button or a separate screen; it is the last recipe in the list, priced like any other.

UPGRADING REPLACES THE STATION IN PLACE. Stated on every tier page in the same words: 'Upgrading the crafting station will replace the workbench with a workbench tier 1.' The node becomes the next node; there is no moment where both exist.

AN UPGRADED STATION IS A SUPERSET AND NEVER LOSES A RECIPE. Tier 2's own description: 'It contains all of the recipes in the workbench tier 1 and other recipes too.' Tier 4 still lists the Wooden Pickaxe at 3 Oak Wood, the very first recipe of the game. Counted from the wiki tables on 2026-09-20, the recipe rows run roughly 55 at tier 1, 139 at tier 2 and 185 at tier 3 — those counts are a measurement of the wiki's tables, not a figure the game states.

THE CATEGORY LIST COUNTS THE UNFILTERED VIEW AS ONE OF ITS CATEGORIES. Tier 4: 'The workbench tier 4’s recipes are sorted into 7 categories: All, tools, blocks, workbenches, utility, factory, and fun.' Tier 3 names the same seven with a weaker verb — 'can be sorted into 7 categories' — which may be the wiki describing its own taxonomy rather than the game's filter; this row quoted both pages as 'are sorted' until 2026-09-20. Seven names, one of which is the unfiltered view. WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT SAY, and what this row asserted anyway: where the filter sits relative to the list, and that it appears because the list got long. The tier 1 and tier 2 pages are simply silent about categories, and a wiki's silence is not the game's absence.

A RECIPE ROW CARRIES A PREREQUISITE COLUMN THAT IS MOSTLY EMPTY. The tables run Image, Name, Recipe, Required skill — and Required skill reads 'None' on the large majority of rows, 'Level 3 Farming' on the Watering Can, 'Level 2 Animal Care' on the Net. The column exists for the minority; deleting it when most rows are None is how a skill-gated recipe becomes a mystery.

A BLOCK CAN BE CRAFTABLE AT SEVERAL STATIONS AT ONCE: the Workbench Tier 1 page notes it is 'the only block that is able to be crafted in 4 different crafting stations', and its own infobox lists five stations under 'crafted with'. A recipe belongs to a SET of stations, not to one.

references.source: https://robloxislands.fandom.com/wiki/Skill_Levels and https://robloxislands.fandom.com/wiki/Tutorial — read on 2026-09-20 through https://robloxislands.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Skill%20Levels&prop=wikitext&format=json and the same call for Tutorial.
demonstrates: ONE LEVEL NUMBER GATES THREE DIFFERENT SCREENS. Levelling a skill gives 'access to new villager trades or crafting recipes, and islands' — the same progression value is read by the trade screen, the crafting screen and the world. A crafting screen that owns its own unlock table will disagree with the other two.

SKILL GROUPS ARE ENCODED BY COLOUR, NOT BY TAB: 'Skills are divided into 3 groups organised by type and differentiated by color: brown, green and red. Brown skills are related to gathering resources/coins. Green skills are aimed at the production of goods... Red skills are related to combat.' Three colours over a longer list of skills, which is a legend a crafting screen can reuse when it shows why a recipe is locked.
THE PROGRESSION SCREEN HAS A KEYBOARD ROUTE AND A TOUCH ROUTE AND THE PAGE STATES BOTH: 'tap on the three bars icon on the left, or tap the J key for PC players.'

THE FIRST CRAFTING SCREEN A NEW PLAYER SEES IS DELIBERATELY REDUCED. The Tutorial page: instead of giving a Workbench Tier 1, the tutorial 'now gives you a Workbench, a type of workbench with only 2 recipes'. Those two are the tool the next tutorial step needs and the upgrade out of the tutorial — a tutorial station is the same screen with a shorter list, not a different screen.

THE TUTORIAL STEP NAMES THE SCREEN AND THE ROW: 'Open your Starter Workbench and craft the Wooden Pickaxe.' The instruction is addressable because the list is two rows long; the same sentence against 185 rows would need a highlight.

references.source: https://bee-swarm-simulator.fandom.com/wiki/Blender — read on 2026-09-20 through https://bee-swarm-simulator.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Blender&prop=wikitext&format=json. Bee Swarm Simulator is a shipped Roblox game; the Blender is its timed crafting machine, with 20 recipes.
demonstrates: THE QUEUE IS ONE RECIPE DEEP AND N ITEMS WIDE: 'the player is only able to craft one type of item at a time', with a quantity selected before starting. There is no multi-recipe queue; there is a selected recipe and a count.

ENDING A QUEUE EARLY SETTLES PARTIALLY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. 'The player can end the crafting process at any time by clicking on the End Crafting button. This will give the player all finished items, and all unfinished items will be turned back into their ingredients and given back to the player.' Cancelling is never a loss — finished output is delivered and unfinished input is refunded. Most crafting screens make the player choose between waiting and losing the batch; this one removes the choice.

THE SAME BUTTON'S COLOUR IS THE COMPLETION STATE: 'If the button is green, then everything has been blended. If not (red button), then the Blender has not finished blending.' One control, two colours, and the colour tells you which of the two settlements you are about to take before you take it.

THE TIMER'S MEANING CHANGES WITH AN OWNED ENTITLEMENT, AND THE SCREEN SAYS SO IN WORDS. Each item takes 5 minutes and 'the timer only counts down when the player is in-game, unless they have an Offline Voucher'. The wiki records the exact string: with the voucher redeemed, the message above the buttons reads "You've redeemed the offline voucher! The blender will continue running for up to 24 hours while you are offline." A status line above the controls, whose text is selected by an entitlement.

THE SPEED-UP PRICE IS A PER-RECIPE RATE, NOT A GLOBAL ONE: 'For every 1 item being crafted, the Blender requires 1 more ticket to speed up. Except for Moon Charm and Gumdrops, for which each ticket serves for speeding up whole 10 items.' Two recipes out of twenty are priced ten times cheaper to rush, so the rush control cannot render a constant.

THE QUANTITY SELECTOR IS NOT CLAMPED TO AFFORDABILITY; THE CONFIRM IS. From the page's own Trivia: leaving and reopening the Blender 'would show that you would select the number of red extracts you want to craft, even if the amount displayed is above the amount you would be able to craft with your resources, though you won't be able to select the Confirm option.' Selecting an impossible amount is allowed and the commit is refused.

THE INGREDIENT LINE IS WRITTEN AS WHAT WILL BE SUBTRACTED, AND THE PLURAL IS BUILT BY APPENDING A LETTER. Trivia records two live spelling defects: a recipe needing two or more strawberries renders as '[-n Strawberrys]', and anything needing enzymes renders as '[-n Enzymess]' — but crafting the enzymes themselves spells it correctly, because that path formats the OUTPUT rather than the ingredient. A shipped game's ingredient label is name-plus-s, and the bracketed minus prefix is the format.

references.source: https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/Skills and https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/How_to_Play — read on 2026-09-20 through https://tds.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Skills&prop=wikitext&format=json and the same call for How%20to%20Play. Tower Defense Simulator is a shipped Roblox game; Skills is its out-of-match upgrade tree.
demonstrates: THE WHOLE TREE IS GATED AS ONE FEATURE, AT Level 15, before any node is. A screen that does not exist yet is a different problem from a node that is not affordable yet, and this game separates them.

FOUR CATEGORIES, SEVENTEEN NODES: Offensive (4), Economy (4), Strategy (4) and Defense (5). Counted from the page on 2026-09-20 the named skills are Enhanced Optics, Improved Gunpowder, Fight Dirty, Precision, Resourcefulness, Bigger Budget, Stonks, Scavenger, Accelerator, Scholar, Expanded Barracks, Re-enforcements, Fortify, Over-Heal, Bandages, Extreme Conditioning and Beefed Up Minions.

A NODE IS A METER WITH ITS OWN CAP, NOT A BINARY UNLOCK. The caps read 10, 15, 20, 25 and 40 across the seventeen skills — Re-enforcements caps at 10, Precision at 15, Fortify at 40 — and the page states the spread in its own prose: 'Each Skill has its own level cap, some being as low as 10 and others having up to 40 levels.' No single progress geometry fits the whole tree, so the cap has to be per node.

THE PREREQUISITE IS A CONSTANT THRESHOLD ON THE PARENT, NOT A FRACTION OF THE PARENT'S CAP. Thirteen of the seventeen skills carry the sentence 'There is a requirement of reaching Level 10 in <named skill> before it is unlocked', and it is Level 10 whether the parent caps at 20, 25 or 40. The tree is therefore a set of short chains inside each category, all with the same unlock depth.

A LEVEL ROW SHOWS THREE THINGS — the price of that level, the cumulative total, and the resulting value — except the first row of a skill, which carries only the price and the value because there is nothing yet to accumulate. Enhanced Optics opens '20 coins • 0.5% total increase' and its second row reads '75 coins • 95 total cost • 1% total increase'. Where the stat counts down rather than up, the third column follows: Precision, the critical-hit skill whose own prerequisite is Level 10 in Fight Dirty, lists '29 shots required' and then 28, 27, 26 as the levels rise.

THE PRICE CURVE IS EXPONENTIAL AND THE PAGE PUBLISHES THE FORMULA — base cost times level, raised to an exponential value, floored and then rounded to the nearest multiple of 5. Prices in a shipped upgrade tree land on round numbers on purpose.

THE RESPEC REFUNDS INTO A CURRENCY THAT CANNOT LEAVE THE TREE. A reset returns 95% of what was spent as Skill Credit, 'a unique currency only usable for Skills'; the reset itself costs 200 Coins and 'each reset will become more expensive by 200'; and after resetting, skills 'are unable to be upgraded using Coins, they are restricted to only Skill Credit' until the credits run out. So the tree has two spend currencies, one of which is a refund that must be spent back into the same screen before the ordinary one is accepted again.

THE TREE'S STATE IS MIRRORED OUTSIDE THE TREE: 'After the player unlocks a Skill from a specific path, a modifier for that path will appear... The description of the modifier will list every single Skill owned and how much it boosts specific statistics.' One chip per category, whose tooltip enumerates every owned node.

THE TREE CAN BE TURNED OFF: Skills have their own toggle in Settings, and certain modes disable them outright. A purchased upgrade that is not in effect this match is a state the match HUD has to be able to say.

THE PROGRESS LIVES ON THE INVENTORY TILE, NOT IN A SEPARATE SCREEN: 'the tower will have a orange progress bar in the inventory, indicating the current level of the tower.' The upgrade state is a bar on the item you already see.

ONLY THE LAST STEP OF THAT BAR MEANS ANYTHING for an unevolved tower — 'the only level that actually matters is the last one, as all others have no impact' — so the bar is progress toward ONE gate, and labelling its intermediate stops as upgrades would be a lie.

THE PLAYER DOES NOT CHOOSE WHICH NODE UNLOCKS: 'The player does not get to pick which upgrades they unlock as each one has a determined level it is unlocked on.' This is the other kind of upgrade tree — a fixed ladder revealed by level — and it needs no affordability state at all, only a reached/not-reached one.

AN EVOLVED TOWER STARTS PARTIALLY UNLOCKED: it 'starts out with only some of its upgrades unlocked', and every upgrade past that set requires levelling. So the same panel renders owned, not-yet-reached and never-available side by side.
THE LADDER HAS A PAID SKIP: the player 'can also skip getting experience with Robux', on both the unevolved and the evolved tower. A level gate with a purchasable bypass is two controls on one node.

LEVEL COUNTS ARE PER TOWER and the page states the observed ceiling as 20 'outside of development screenshots', with experience per level computed from a base value and a growth rate raised to level minus one, rounded down.

references.source: https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Upgrades — read on 2026-09-20 through https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Team%20Upgrades&prop=wikitext&format=json. Roblox BedWars is a shipped Roblox game; the page carries the wiki's Outdated banner. THE MAIN TABLE IS NOT A CURRENT TABLE, AND THIS LINE SAID IT WAS UNTIL 2026-09-20: its last column is headed 'Date Of Removal', and five of its eleven upgrade entries carry a date — Iron Arrows, Charging Gloops and Healing Fountain on April 5, 2024, the three Mining tiers on April 28, 2023, and Armory on June 23, 2023. The six reading N/A are Team Generator, Armor Protection, Damage, Diamond Generator, Break Speed/Destruction and Enchant Table. Below that the page carries a Season 10/11 table and a Season 9 table under a 'Removed' heading. Each claim below names which table it came from and whether its row is dated removed.
demonstrates: THE UPGRADE SCREEN IS A PLACE AND A PERSON: the menu 'can be accessed by interacting with Fulco, who can be found in each team's base'. Like a shop keeper, the tree is reached by walking to it rather than by a button on the HUD.

TIERS OF ONE UPGRADE SHARE A NAME AND AN ICON AND DIFFER BY A TIER NUMBER AND A PRICE. Team Generator is one entry with tiers 1, 2 and 3 at 4, 8 and 16 diamonds; Armor Protection is one entry with tiers 1–4 at 4, 8, 20 and 500. The cost escalates roughly by doubling and then breaks. How the wiki DRAWS that grouping — one icon cell spanning the tier rows — is the table's own rowspan markup and is not recorded here as anything about the game's screen.

UNTIERED ONE-SHOT UNLOCKS SIT IN THE SAME LIST WITH THE TIER COLUMN READING 'None' — Armory, Healing Fountain, Enchant Table, Iron Arrows, Charging Gloops. A tree therefore contains both multi-step nodes and single-step nodes and cannot assume every node has a next step. FOUR OF THOSE FIVE ARE DATED REMOVED in the table's own 'Date Of Removal' column — Iron Arrows, Charging Gloops and Healing Fountain on April 5, 2024, Armory on June 23, 2023 — and only Enchant Table reads N/A beside the five tiered entries. The mixed-shape list is therefore mostly a record of what BedWars used to sell, and one untiered node survives in it.

A TIER CAN BE CONDITIONAL ON THE MODE: tier 4 of Armor Protection, Damage and Destruction each read '4 (Hyper Gen only)'. The node exists in one mode and not in another, which is a different absence from unaffordable or unreached.

BUYING A NODE RETROACTIVELY CHANGES ITEMS ALREADY HELD: Iron Arrows 'unlocks iron arrows and upgrades any arrows already in the inventory', and Charging Gloops does the same for gloops. The inventory screen has to re-render on an upgrade purchase made in a different screen. Both rows are dated removed April 5, 2024 in the same table, so this is a mechanism BedWars shipped and then withdrew, not one a player can trigger today.

A NODE'S PAYLOAD CAN BE ROWS IN ANOTHER SCREEN: the Armory upgrade 'unlocks several combat items inside of the Item Shop', and the Brewing Stand row of the removed Season 9 table 'Unlocks 5 Unique Potions inside of the Item Shop'. The locked state for those items lives in the shop, not in the tree. BOTH SOURCES ARE HISTORICAL: Armory is dated June 23, 2023 in the main table's removal column, and the Brewing Stand row sits inside the table the page files under 'Removed'.

COMPOUND PREREQUISITES ARE REAL AND WERE PUBLISHED AS THEIR OWN COLUMN. In the Season 9 table — which the page presents as REMOVED, so this is a historical system — the prerequisites read 'None', 'Iron Era', 'Diamond Era', 'Diamond Era + Destruction I', 'Emerald Era + Magic I', 'Diamond Era + Altar I'. A spine of three Eras, and branches (Destruction, Magic, Altar, Bed Defense) each of whose steps needs both the next Era AND the previous step of its own branch.
THE SPINE NODES ADVERTISE WHAT THEY OPEN, NOT ONLY WHAT THEY GIVE: Iron Era 'unlocks iron-related armory, the crossbow, and two upgrades'. A prerequisite node's description counts the doors it opens.

references.source: https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/wiki/Forge — read on 2026-09-20 through https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Forge&prop=wikitext&format=json. The page is marked as a removed feature (removed November 17, 2023), which is why the claims below are recorded as a shipped design that existed rather than as current behaviour.
demonstrates: THE CLOSEST THING ANY SOURCE HERE GIVES TO AN AFFORDABILITY READOUT: 'The forge displays how many upgrades are currently available based on the player's current forge point count.' The screen states a COUNT of what you can buy right now, rather than leaving the player to scan the tree for a node they can afford. It says how many, not which — that is the limit of what the page states.

EVERY BRANCH IS THE SAME LADDER AND THE PRICE CURVE IS NOT LINEAR: all ten branches — Sword, Dao, Frosty Hammer, Dagger, Scythe, Great Hammer, Gauntlet, Ranged, Armor and Chicken — run six paid levels costing 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 Forge Points, and the seven melee branches carry a preceding row whose level and cost both read 'None' for the default weapon. Uniform depth and uniform price across every branch, with the jump from 4 to 6 to 8 at the top. HOW THE WIKI DRAWS THOSE LEVELS — its Level column is repeated star glyphs with a skull for the top one — IS THE TABLE'S OWN NOTATION AND IS NOT RECORDED HERE AS THE GAME'S SCREEN. The page's own prose numbers them instead, 'depending on forge level (Lvl 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Titan)'. Until 2026-09-20 this row reported the stars as the game's rendering, which is the error the limits below forbid and which the adjacent rowspan case had already been corrected for.

A NODE THAT CLOSES OTHER DOORS SAYS SO IN ITS OWN TEXT. The first sword upgrade reads '+5% Sword Damage + Locks in Sword class + Unlocks Iron Sword', and the prose confirms it: 'Once a tool is picked, it cannot be changed, and the player can only use that weapon type for the rest of the game, excluding bows and armor.' The irreversibility is part of the node's description, not a warning dialog.

SOME BRANCHES COST A POINT JUST TO ENTER: Sword, Ranged, Armor and the kit-locked weapons have Requirements 'None', while Dagger, Scythe, Great Hammer and Gauntlet share a single '1 Forge Point' requirement to select at all. Entry cost and upgrade cost are different numbers on the same node.

A NODE'S PAYLOAD VARIES BY LOADOUT: the three-star sword row unlocks the Diamond Sword generally, the Infernal Saber for one kit and the Light Sword for another. One node, one price, different result depending on who bought it.

references.source: https://99-nights-in-the-forest.fandom.com/wiki/Crafting and https://99-nights-in-the-forest.fandom.com/wiki/Crafting_Blueprint — read on 2026-09-20 through https://99-nights-in-the-forest.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Crafting&prop=wikitext&format=json and the same call for Crafting%20Blueprint. 99 Nights in the Forest is a shipped Roblox survival game.
demonstrates: A PER-RUN CRAFT CAP IS A BADGE ON THE RECIPE, STATED BY THE PAGE AS A SHAPE: 'Some of these items have a white circle with a certain number inside, indicating how many of a certain item can be crafted during a run.' Not every recipe has one, so the badge is conditional and the card must reserve room for it.

THE CAP HAS THREE CASES AND THE LIST USES ALL THREE: a finite limit ('Can be crafted up to 20 times' on the Farm Plot, 'up to eight times' on the Bear Trap, 'up to ten times' on the Torch), unlimited ('Can be placed down more than once', 'You can make an infinite amount'), and the implicit one-off. A recipe row that only knows affordable/unaffordable cannot say any of this.

MATERIAL YIELD IS SHOWN AS REPEATED ICONS WHOSE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE AMOUNT. The page spells the mapping out: one bolt is 1 scrap, two bolts is 3, three bolts is 5, four bolts is 8 — and states the caveat outright, 'the number of symbols doesn't match the quantity you get'. A shipped game chose an ordinal rank over a number, and told players the rank is not a count.

THE STATION'S UPGRADE IS A ROW IN ITS OWN LIST, at every tier: 'Crafting Bench 2' is priced 5 Wood 1 Scrap inside the tier 1 list, 'Crafting Bench 3' is 15 Wood 10 Scrap inside tier 2, 'Crafting Bench Tier 4' is 30 Wood 20 Scrap 2 Cultist Gems inside tier 3, 'Crafting Bench Tier 5' is 50 Wood 50 Scrap 1 Gem of the Forest inside tier 4. Independent confirmation of the same convention Islands uses.

THE LADDER INTRODUCES A NEW CURRENCY AT THE TOP RATHER THAN SCALING THE OLD ONE. Tiers 1–3 are priced in Wood and Scrap only; tier 4 adds Cultist Gems; tier 5 adds Gem of the Forest. The price row therefore grows a slot partway up the tree.

CRAFTING DOES NOT PRODUCE THE OBJECT — IT PRODUCES A PLACEMENT TOKEN. The Crafting Blueprint page: blueprints are 'items that can be in your inventory that can be used to place down various craftables', obtained 'by building items in the Crafting Bench'. Placement is a separate step with its own controls; the page's tips include 'Press R to rotate structures before you place them.'

THE FIRST TIER IS PRESENT FROM THE START AND CARRIES THE ONE THING THE RUN NEEDS. The page, verbatim including its typo: 'The Tier 1 crafting bench is autimatically in when you start a world. It also contains the most important blueprint: the map.'

A RECIPE'S PRICE IS A LIST OF RESOURCE CHIPS, NOT A SINGLE NUMBER — most rows carry two (Wood and Scrap), the top tiers three. The wiki's own summary of buying everything once, 423 Wood, 419 Scrap, 6 Cultist Gems and 5 Gems of the Forest, is a count it computed rather than a figure the game shows.

references.source: https://deadrails.fandom.com/wiki/Crafting — read on 2026-09-20 through https://deadrails.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Crafting&prop=wikitext&format=json. Dead Rails is a shipped Roblox game; crafting was added in the Crafting & Traveling Merchant update of 28 February 2026.
demonstrates: CRAFTING LIVES BETWEEN RUNS, NOT IN THEM: resources are deposited at Fortified Towns during a run and 'players can use these resources to craft items in the Lobby to use in later games'. The crafting screen belongs to the lobby and its output is next run's loadout.

EVERY RESOURCE CARRIES ITS OWN CAP AND THE CAPS DIFFER: 'With the exception of Components (which has a 15 limit), all other resources have a limit of 30.' A resource counter in this screen is a value against a maximum, and the maximum is per resource, so one shared 'x / 30' chip would be wrong for one of the six.
THE DEPOSIT ITSELF IS CAPPED PER SESSION — 'players can deposit up to 5 items per game session' — so the screen that feeds the crafting screen has a budget of its own.

A RECORDED LAYOUT DEFECT WORTH DESIGNING AGAINST: 'When obtaining special resources, it will display it in yellow text below the basic resources obtained from depositing. Players may have to scroll down to see what they have obtained.' The rarest outcome is rendered last and in a different colour, below the fold of its own summary panel.

A RECIPE CAN BE LISTED AND STILL NEED A FOUND BLUEPRINT: the Skeleton Grenade row is annotated '(requires Blueprint)' and links to the dungeon it comes from. So the list shows recipes the player cannot craft and names the missing precondition on the row.

ONE ROW CAN COVER A FAMILY OF OUTPUTS AT ONE PRICE: Light Ammo, Medium Ammo and Shotgun Shells share a row at 6 Wood, and Revolver, Rifle and Shotgun share a row at 4 Wood, 1 Component and 10 Metal. The recipe is the cost, and the output is a choice made inside it.

RESOURCES ARE SPLIT INTO TWO NAMED CLASSES — four Basic (Wood, Metal, Linen, Component) and two Special (Holy Metal, Bone Fragment) — and the split is what the yellow-text treatment above is keyed to.

references.source: https://deepwoken.fandom.com/wiki/Attribute_Trees — read on 2026-09-20 through https://deepwoken.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Attribute%20Trees&prop=wikitext&format=json. Deepwoken is a shipped Roblox RPG. THE PAGE CARRIES THE WIKI'S OWN 'Outdated' BANNER and states it has documented 71 of about 200 talent trees, so it is recorded here for the SHAPE of its prerequisites rather than for any particular talent.
demonstrates: A PREREQUISITE IS A LIST OF CLAUSES AND AT LEAST ONE CLAUSE CAN BE A DISJUNCTION. The page's worked example writes Potion Quaffer's prerequisites as '[15 Fortitude OR 15 Willpower, 30 intelligence, Other]' — an AND of clauses, one of which is an OR of two attribute thresholds, plus a catch-all clause named 'Other'. A requirement row that can only render 'needs X' cannot render that.

A NODE WITH A DISJUNCTIVE PREREQUISITE BELONGS TO MORE THAN ONE BRANCH AT ONCE, and the page says such a talent appears under every attribute it involves. A tree drawn as a strict hierarchy has nowhere to put it.

THE DEEPEST NODES ARE DEFINED BY DEPTH, NOT BY PRICE: Advanced talents 'are often at the end of a Talent tree, requiring various other Talents as prerequisites' and are described as 'not rare if you meet the requirements'. Scarcity here is prerequisite depth rather than cost or drop rate.

THE TREE HAS A SLOT BUDGET WITH NAMED EXEMPTIONS, AND THE FOUR EXEMPT GROUPS ARE NOT WORDED ALIKE. The Race/Aspect, Origin/Quest and Mantra Level/Mastery entries each read 'These Talents do not take up Talent slots'; the Oath/Memento entry reads 'They relate to the Oath taken and don’t take up Talent slots'. This row put the longer wording in all four mouths until 2026-09-20. The Mastery ones are also 'granted instantly upon meeting their prerequisites'. So a node can enter the tree without being chosen and without being counted. The same section lists Faction talents, but says only how they are awarded — 'as a reward from having high reputation or completing a specific milestone or task for a faction' — and says nothing about slots, so Faction is not part of this claim.

THE ACQUISITION SURFACE IS NOT THE TREE. Talents arrive as a HAND of cards at each power-up; a 'Fold' card 'removes your current hand of cards' and rerolls at the next power-up, and after folding three times in one power-up 'all remaining talent hands will be skipped and will roll over to your next Power up'. The prerequisite graph exists and is browsable, but the player never clicks a node in it — a separation worth knowing before assuming every upgrade tree is also its own purchase screen.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/3006528 — read on 2026-09-20 through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/3006528.json, Discourse's own JSON endpoint for the topic. An Art Design Support thread from 2024-06-06 on a crafting menu — the topic's category_id is 57, resolved against devforum.roblox.com/site.json — in which the author posted six screenshots of the screen across the thread, at posts 1, 5, 8, 10, 15 and 18: the original plus five revisions.
demonstrates: THE REGIONS MUST BE LABELLED IN THE UI, NOT IN AN ANNOTATION. The author posted a second, annotated image explaining what each region was, and the first reply's point was exactly that: 'without the Red texts, players are required to learn alone for a few seconds before understanding what the whole crafting menu is doing', followed by the proposed labels — 'Inventory', 'Craftable Items', 'Ingredients required'.

A CRAFTING SCREEN IS MISTAKABLE FOR A SHOP WITHOUT A TITLE. A second reviewer, quoted as posted: 'Or at least add a title telling peole that this is infacet a crafting menue and not a shop or somthing.' The misspellings are his; this row silently corrected them until 2026-09-20, which turns a quotation into a paraphrase wearing quotation marks. The two screens share a grid of priced things, and the title is what separates them.

READING ORDER WAS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE LAYOUT, AND IT WAS MADE ONCE AND THEN SECONDED. One reviewer: 'as a minecraft player- Im used to the output being on the right. I feel like it makes more sence that way because you also read left to right.' The next reply asks to 'Change the order of the crafting menu, so ingredients go first, like other people have mentioned' — it names no reason of its own and says outright that it is agreeing with an earlier post. The author then posted a revision saying he had taken everyone's advice, but WHAT HE CHANGED IS IN AN IMAGE THIS FILE CANNOT SEE — the reorder is reported, not observed, and this row asserted it flatly until 2026-09-20. The reviewer who gave the reason invoked it a second time later in the thread, for the placement of an item's name against its materials line.

THE MISSING INGREDIENTS BELONG ON THE RECIPE ROW, not in a distant panel: 'you could also move the missing ingredients. you could put it under the name of the item in the "things the player can craft" section'.

SELECTING A RECIPE SHOULD GHOST ITS INGREDIENTS INTO THE SLOTS: 'Make clicking the items that are able to be crafted at the top leave transparent hints inside the crafting spaces.' The slot shows what it wants before you have it.

AN INGREDIENT SLOT CAN ACCEPT A CLASS OF ITEM, AND THE HINT HAS TO SAY SO. The author's own caption on the revision that added hints: 'The multi-colored log in the hint just represents any kind of log.' A ghost that shows one specific item would be a lie about what the slot accepts.

THE INGREDIENT LIST IS A LAYOUT OF CHIPS, NOT ONE TEXT LINE. The author was using TextScaled on a single label and hit the wall himself — 'the ingredients can sometimes be a list of items, and having that text on the same text box might look weird if it ends up on multiple lines' — and a reviewer's fix, quoted as posted, was 'I though you would be using a gid layout for like a list so you could add more matterials to the list if needed'. The author answered 'I never thought about that. I’ll try to adapt it to work for a grid layout' and an hour later said he had 'Got something decent working'. What he got is a screenshot this file's reader cannot see; the grid is reported, not observed.

THE REQUIREMENT HEADING WANTS TO BE SHORT: 'instead of it saying "Materials Needed:" it could say "Made With:" or "Requires:" just to make that text shorter' — so the name of the item and the name of its requirements are competing for the same width, which is also why a reviewer asked that the requirement text be smaller than the item name.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/449252 — read on 2026-09-20 through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/449252.json. An Art Design Support thread from 2020-02-02 titled 'Crafting UI design thoughts?', in which the author states the intended behaviour of his own crafting screen.
demonstrates: THE AUTHOR'S OWN STATEMENT OF THE THREE-REGION FLOW, which matches the 2024 thread four years later and from a different author: 'the grid boxes would be the stuff they can craft. They'd click the item they wanna craft, then the stuff in the middle would change depending on what items a player has, if they have all the right items, the craft button lights up, and they can craft it.' Select in a grid, requirements resolve in the middle against what you hold, and the commit control changes state — it LIGHTS UP rather than un-greys, which is the only statement of a locked-to-affordable transition anywhere in this file, and it is a developer describing intent, not a shipped rendering.
THE PLAYER'S INVENTORY IS PART OF THE CRAFTING SCREEN: 'The boxes at the bottom is the players inventory.' The thing you are spending and the thing you are buying are on one surface.

A REQUIREMENTS HEADING WAS MISSING AND THE THREAD NOTICED: 'You might be best off putting a bold “requirements” about the ingredients just to make it fit in a bit more, its currently looks a bit out of place.' The author replied that he had 'Added an underline to the Requirements, not too sure about it tho', and the next reviewer rejected the underline — 'The line looks extremely off and really takes away from the style of the other UI, id say go without it, and just end up always making the important text bold.' HOW IT ENDED IS NOT IN THE THREAD. The author's next post is a screenshot with no text, which nobody reading this JSON can see, and the last word on the question is a 2022 reply saying 'I like the line personally.' This row said bold was how the heading was settled until 2026-09-20; nothing on the page settles it.

A SCROLLBAR WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT READS AS BROKEN: 'the scrollbar for the things on the left is just floating and is a wee bit offputting. Put the whitebackground behind it or put it in its own background with a darker grey.' The recipe list's scroll track needs its own surface.

THE SPACING BETWEEN THE HEADER BAR AND THE CONTENT SHEET WAS THE ONE MEASURED DEFECT: 'The distance between the brown bar at the top and the white bit below it isn't the same as the rest of the UI, just need to increase it 2-3 pixels or so.' Nobody in the thread measured anything else.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/2835392 — read on 2026-09-20 through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/2835392.json. A Scripting Support thread from a developer whose crafting screen handed out every craftable item at once, with the accepted diagnosis in the first reply.
demonstrates: THE CRAFTING PANEL DECOMPOSES INTO THREE NAMED CHILDREN AND ONE BUTTON, in the author's own instance names: RecipesFrame, RequirementsFrame, CraftFrame — and inside CraftFrame a single CraftButton. One commit control for the whole screen, not one per recipe row.

THE TRAP A GENERATOR WILL HIT, NAMED EXACTLY: the author connected the single craft button inside the loop over recipe buttons, so clicking it fired every recipe's handler. The accepted fix is the missing piece of state: 'making a variable that stores the current selected recipe, and when you click the craft button, it uses the current selected one.' A crafting screen needs a selected-recipe variable; a shop grid, where every tile owns its own buy button, does not.

THE SHELL IS THE SAME SHELL AS A SHOP: an Open button outside the panel setting BG.Visible true, and a Close button inside it setting it false — which is the structure screen-shop.json records for the shop's opener, arrived at independently here.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/3090458 — read on 2026-09-20 through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/3090458.json. A Creations Feedback thread on a survival game's inventory-and-crafting screen, the author naming Muck, Raft and Terraria as its references.
demonstrates: THE SCREEN CARRIES TWO NAMED SECTIONS SIDE BY SIDE — 'Backpack' and 'Hand Crafting' — so the recipes you can make with no station are part of the inventory screen rather than a station screen.

ONE REVIEWER ASKED FOR SEARCH AND GAVE A REASON; THE NEXT REPLY SECONDED IT AND GAVE NONE. The first: 'I do think the hand-crafting UI could be a bit complicated for people who are trying to look for specific recipes. Maybe adding a search mechanic could help?' The second closes with 'Adding on to the person above me yeah you should add a search bar above the crafting area' — it states that it is building on the post above and names no reason of its own. The author replied 'I'll see what I can do about a searching feature, but that will be for later when I finish scripting everything.' A recipe list long enough to scroll is a list somebody is hunting in, but that is one person's stated reason on one unreleased project.
THE INGREDIENT READOUT FORMAT IN USE IS name-space-x-space-count — the reviewer quotes the on-screen text as 'Wood x 1' when discussing its colour.

THE AUTHOR MEASURED READABILITY RATHER THAN ARGUING IT: told to make everything bigger, he replied that 'The Gui looks small in Studio but it's very readable when actually playing', tested on a 27 inch monitor and a 15 inch laptop. A crafting screen judged in the Studio viewport is judged at the wrong size.

THE TEXT COLOUR ADVICE SPLITS BY ROLE: section titles in a tinted colour with a drop shadow, and the numeric item text — the '999', the 'Wood x 1' — plain white. Counts read as data, headings read as chrome.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/1000046 — read on 2026-09-20 through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/1000046.json. A showcase thread opened 2021-01-22, titled 'Unique Skill Tree', for a project the author states will carry upwards of 750 abilities; the construction detail below is the author's answer to a direct question about how it was built, and his own follow-up two years later reverses it. The topic's category_id is 20, which resolves against devforum.roblox.com/site.json — the lookup this file's provenance describes — to 'Creations Feedback', the same category as topic 3090458. This line called it 'Cool Creations' until 2026-09-20, which is not what that lookup returns.
demonstrates: THE EDGES ARE THE HARD PART; THIS AUTHOR SOLVED THEM OUTSIDE THE GUI AND THEN UNDID IT. Post 9, in 2021: 'The tree itself isn’t a GUI but bricks using beams to connect them, from there you can use the beams to figure out what point goes where, you can then get creative with the effects by tweening the points and using the beams properties.' A curved, animatable connector between two nodes is what drove that tree out of a ScreenGui and into 3D parts. POST 15 OF THE SAME TOPIC, BY THE SAME AUTHOR, ON 2023-02-14: 'I ended up making a completely 2D version of this skill tree, and I’m very happy with the results!' He gives no reason and attaches a video this file's reader cannot see. So beams are a real route to a curved edge and NOT a settled verdict — the one developer who took it did not stay there, and this file recorded only the first half of him until 2026-09-20.

THE AUTHOR'S STATED PROBLEM WITH EXISTING TREES IS ORGANISATION, NOT LOOKS: 'a common issue I notice in games is the lack of organization as well as overall visual appeal', against 750 abilities. At that size the tree's job is navigation.

THE SECOND DESIGN CONSTRAINT CAME FROM THE AUTHORING SIDE: the difficult part was 'making it able to be easily customizable and allowing the developers to create skill trees with virtually no programming knowledge'. A tree whose node graph is not data is a tree nobody re-balances.

A REVIEWER STATED THE DEPTH TRADE-OFF PLAINLY: trees 'should be deep enough to feel like you can have an impact on your gameplay and style' while not being complicated — which is the same tension TDS resolves with four short chains rather than one long one.

rules.rule: Build the requirement block from three axes — materials, a level or skill gate, and a currency price — and keep the gate and the price on screen even when they read zero.
rules.why: Fisch's recipes vary independently: the Vineweaver Rod is Level 0 at 150,000 C$, the Rod of the Eternal King is Level 400 at 0 C$. Islands' recipe tables carry a 'Required skill' column that reads None on most rows and 'Level 3 Farming' on one. A block that only draws the axes in play changes shape between two rows of the same list. The zero case is demonstrated for the level gate and for the price and NOT for materials — no recipe on the Fisch page has an empty material list — so nothing here says what a recipe that costs no materials should look like.

rules.rule: Treat an ingredient as an item PLUS its variant, and show the variant on the chip.
rules.why: Fisch's rod recipes call for six different Driftwoods as six different ingredients — Mythical, Lunar, Frozen, Atlantean, Poisoned, Vined — and separately Spirit Sea Mine and Spirit Speed Core; the page's ingredient index carries nine Driftwood rows in all. A crafting screen that matches inventory by base item will tell a player they have an ingredient they do not have.

rules.rule: Write the ingredient line as what will be SUBTRACTED, and never build its plural by appending a letter to the item name.
rules.why: Bee Swarm's Blender renders ingredient cost as a bracketed negative, and its own wiki records two live defects from naive pluralisation — '[-n Strawberrys]' and '[-n Enzymess]' — while the same item spells correctly when it is the OUTPUT, because that path formats a different string. The minus prefix is worth copying; the plural is worth fixing.

rules.rule: Put the station's own upgrade in the station's recipe list, priced like any other recipe.
rules.why: Islands' starter workbench has exactly two recipes and one of them is Workbench Tier 1 at 5 Oak Wood and 2 Iron Ore; 99 Nights in the Forest does the same at all four steps, Crafting Bench 2 inside tier 1 and so on up to tier 5. Two unrelated shipped games reached the same convention, and it means the upgrade needs no second surface.

rules.rule: An upgraded station is a superset. Never remove a recipe on the way up.
rules.why: Islands states it outright — tier 2 'contains all of the recipes in the workbench tier 1 and other recipes too' — and tier 4 still lists the Wooden Pickaxe at 3 Oak Wood. A player who upgraded and lost a recipe has been punished for progressing.

rules.rule: Make the upgrade replace the station in place, so there is never a moment when both exist.
rules.why: Every Islands tier page repeats the same sentence: 'Upgrading the crafting station will replace the workbench with a workbench tier 1.' Leaving the old station standing beside the new one turns a linear ladder into an inventory problem.

rules.rule: Ship the first crafting screen with a short list, not a filtered long one.
rules.why: Islands' tutorial hands out a starter workbench 'with only 2 recipes' — the tool the next tutorial step needs and the upgrade out of the tutorial — where the same station at tier 3 carries a list long enough to need seven categories. Same screen, shorter list, and the tutorial line 'Open your Starter Workbench and craft the Wooden Pickaxe' is addressable because of it.

rules.rule: When a recipe list carries a category filter, count the unfiltered view as one of the categories.
rules.why: Islands' workbench tier 4 page states that its 'recipes are sorted into 7 categories: All, tools, blocks, workbenches, utility, factory, and fun', and the tier 3 page names the same seven with 'can be sorted'. 'All' is one of the seven rather than a control beside them, which is the whole of what the source supports. Two things this reason claimed until 2026-09-20 are gone: where the filter is drawn, which no page states, and that the row arrives with list length, which was read off the tier 1 and tier 2 pages saying nothing about categories at all.

rules.rule: Give a scrolling recipe list a search field.
rules.why: In one DevForum feedback thread on an unreleased survival game, a search field was the only thing two different repliers both asked for, and one of them gave the reason: the hand-crafting UI 'could be a bit complicated for people who are trying to look for specific recipes'. The second reply opens 'Adding on to the person above me' and names no reason, so this rule rests on one stated reason from one reviewer looking at one screenshot — not on two independent ones.

rules.rule: Label every region of the crafting screen in the UI itself, and give the screen a title that says it is a crafting screen.
rules.why: The 2024 crafting-menu thread opened with the author posting a SECOND annotated image to explain his regions, and the first reply's point was that without those annotations 'players are required to learn alone for a few seconds'. A later reviewer went further, in his own spelling: 'Or at least add a title telling peole that this is infacet a crafting menue and not a shop or somthing.' A crafting grid and a shop grid look alike.

rules.rule: Order the screen ingredients-then-output, left to right.
rules.why: One reviewer argued it from reading order — 'Im used to the output being on the right... because you also read left to right' — and the next reply asked for the same reorder while crediting earlier posts rather than giving a reason. The author posted a revision saying he had taken the advice; what it looks like is a screenshot, so the reorder is reported rather than seen, and the same reviewer was still asking for a swap of the name and the materials line two posts later. It is the only layout question in the file settled by an argument rather than by taste, but the argument was made once and seconded, not made twice.

rules.rule: Render the ingredient requirement as a layout of chips, not one scaled text line.
rules.why: The author who used TextScaled on a single label hit the wall himself — 'the ingredients can sometimes be a list of items, and having that text on the same text box might look weird if it ends up on multiple lines' — and said he would 'adapt it to work for a grid layout' when a reviewer pointed out a list can grow, then reported it working — the result is a screenshot, so the rebuild is reported rather than seen. Fisch's recipes run up to four ingredients and Bee Swarm's up to four, so the list does grow.

rules.rule: On selecting a recipe, ghost its ingredients into the slots — and when a slot accepts a CLASS of item, make the ghost show the class.
rules.why: A reviewer asked for 'transparent hints inside the crafting spaces', and the author's own caption on the revision that added them is the important half: 'The multi-colored log in the hint just represents any kind of log.' A ghost showing one specific item would misstate what the slot accepts.

rules.rule: One craft button for the screen, driven by a stored selected-recipe value — not one button per recipe row.
rules.why: A Scripting Support thread exists because its author connected the single craft button inside the loop over recipe rows, and crafting one item handed out every item. The accepted fix is literally the missing state: a variable holding the current selected recipe. This is where a crafting screen diverges from a shop grid, in which every tile legitimately owns its own buy button.

rules.rule: Let the quantity stepper go above what the player can afford, and refuse at the commit instead of clamping.
rules.why: Bee Swarm's Blender does exactly this, and its own wiki records the consequence: reopening the machine shows a selected count 'above the amount you would be able to craft with your resources, though you won't be able to select the Confirm option'. Clamping the stepper hides how short you are; refusing the commit shows it.

rules.rule: A timed crafting queue holds ONE recipe and a count, and ending it early settles partially — finished output delivered, unfinished input refunded.
rules.why: Bee Swarm's Blender: 'the player is only able to craft one type of item at a time', and End Crafting 'will give the player all finished items, and all unfinished items will be turned back into their ingredients and given back to the player'. This is the strongest crafting decision found: most queues make the player choose between waiting and losing the batch, and this one deletes the choice, which is why the cancel control can sit in the open instead of behind a confirm.

rules.rule: Put the queue's completion state in the colour of the control that ends it.
rules.why: Bee Swarm again: 'If the button is green, then everything has been blended. If not (red button), then the Blender has not finished blending.' One control, two colours, and the colour tells the player which of the two settlements they are about to take before they take it.

rules.rule: When an entitlement changes what the timer MEANS, say so in a status line above the controls.
rules.why: The Blender's timer only counts down while the player is in-game unless an Offline Voucher is redeemed, and the wiki records the exact replacement string shown above the buttons in that case. A countdown whose rules changed silently is a countdown the player will misread once and stop trusting.

rules.rule: Price a speed-up per recipe, not per screen.
rules.why: The Blender charges one ticket per item rushed, 'except for Moon Charm and Gumdrops, for which each ticket serves for speeding up whole 10 items' — two of twenty recipes at a tenth the rate. A rush control that renders a constant will be wrong on those two.

rules.rule: Show a per-run or per-save craft cap as a badge on the recipe, and support three cases: a finite number, unlimited, and one-off.
rules.why: 99 Nights in the Forest describes the badge as 'a white circle with a certain number inside, indicating how many of a certain item can be crafted during a run', and its own list uses all three cases — 20 Farm Plots, 8 Bear Traps, 10 Torches, 'an infinite amount' of Shelves and Log Walls. A card that only knows affordable and unaffordable cannot say any of this.

rules.rule: If a count is shown as repeated icons rather than a number, say what the icons mean.
rules.why: 99 Nights shows material yield as repeated bolt glyphs and states plainly that 'the number of symbols doesn't match the quantity you get' — one glyph is 1 scrap, two is 3, three is 5, four is 8. A shipped game chose an ordinal rank over a number and then published the mapping, which is the only thing that makes the rank usable.

rules.rule: Give every resource counter its own maximum, and never assume one cap fits the row.
rules.why: Dead Rails caps Components at 15 and the other five resources at 30, and caps deposits at 5 items per session on top of that. A shared 'x / 30' chip would be wrong for one of the six, and the one it is wrong about is the scarcest.

rules.rule: Do not render the rarest result last and below the fold of its own summary.
rules.why: Dead Rails' own wiki records it as a problem: special resources 'display in yellow text below the basic resources obtained from depositing. Players may have to scroll down to see what they have obtained.' The result the player most wants to see is the one the panel hides.

rules.rule: List recipes the player cannot yet make, and name the missing precondition on the row.
rules.why: Dead Rails annotates the Skeleton Grenade row '(requires Blueprint)' and links the dungeon it drops from; Fisch's material list points at a quest for the Evil Sigil. A recipe hidden until its precondition is met teaches nothing; a recipe shown with its precondition named is a goal.

rules.rule: Let one recipe row cover a family of outputs at one price when the cost is identical.
rules.why: Dead Rails prices Light Ammo, Medium Ammo and Shotgun Shells as one row at 6 Wood, and Revolver, Rifle and Shotgun as one row at 4 Wood, 1 Component and 10 Metal. Three rows carrying the same numbers is three chances to disagree.

rules.rule: Gate the whole tree as one feature before gating any node inside it.
rules.why: Tower Defense Simulator unlocks Skills at player Level 15, and Fisch's crafting altar sits behind a world puzzle before any recipe's level gate applies. A screen that does not exist yet is a different message from a node you cannot afford yet, and collapsing the two produces a tree full of locks with no explanation.

rules.rule: Make a node a meter with its own cap, not a binary unlock, and put its prerequisite at a constant depth on the parent.
rules.why: In TDS, seventeen skills cap at 10, 15, 20, 25 or 40 levels, and thirteen of them carry the same sentence — 'There is a requirement of reaching Level 10 in <named skill> before it is unlocked' — regardless of whether that parent caps at 20, 25 or 40. The unlock depth is a constant, which is what keeps the chains inside each category comparable.

rules.rule: On a levelled node, show three numbers per step: this step's price, the cumulative total, and the resulting value.
rules.why: TDS publishes exactly that per level — '75 coins, 95 total cost, 1% total increase' — and where the stat counts down, the third column follows it down ('29 shots required', then 28, 27). Without the cumulative figure the player cannot compare a node against a node; without the resulting value they cannot compare a node against nothing.

rules.rule: Refund a respec into a currency that can only be spent back into the same tree, and escalate the price of resetting.
rules.why: TDS returns 95% as Skill Credit, 'a unique currency only usable for Skills', charges 200 Coins to reset and states the escalation in its own sentence — 'Each reset will become more expensive by 200.', and refuses ordinary Coins in the tree until the credits are exhausted. The refund cannot leak into the rest of the economy and the escalation prices the optionality — this is the clearest worked respec in the file, and the part worth arguing with is the forced ordering, not the percentage.

rules.rule: Mirror the tree's purchases into ONE summary outside the tree.
rules.why: In TDS, unlocking any skill on a path makes a modifier for that path appear, and 'The description of the modifier will list every single Skill owned and how much it boosts specific statistics'. One chip per category, enumerating the nodes — so a player in a match can check what they bought without reopening the tree.

rules.rule: State how many nodes are affordable right now.
rules.why: BedWars' Forge 'displays how many upgrades are currently available based on the player's current forge point count'. It is the only affordability readout any source read here describes, and it answers the question a tree screen is actually opened to answer — is there anything I can do — without making the player scan for it.

rules.rule: If buying a node closes other doors, write that into the node's own description.
rules.why: BedWars' first sword upgrade reads '+5% Sword Damage + Locks in Sword class + Unlocks Iron Sword', and the page confirms 'once a tool is picked, it cannot be changed'. The irreversibility is on the node, where it is read before the click, rather than in a confirm dialog after it.

rules.rule: Support tiered nodes and one-shot nodes in the same list, and let the tier column read None.
rules.why: BedWars' team upgrade list runs Team Generator at tiers 1-3 (4, 8, 16 diamonds) beside Armory, Healing Fountain and Enchant Table with no tier at all. A tree that assumes every node has a next step cannot render half of this list. Of the five untiered rows only Enchant Table has no removal date: Armory is dated June 23, 2023 and Healing Fountain, Iron Arrows and Charging Gloops April 5, 2024. One current untiered node beside five current tiered ones still makes the shape real, and the list that shows it off best is the one BedWars has since cut down.

rules.rule: Model prerequisites as expressions, not as a parent pointer: AND across clauses, OR inside one.
rules.why: BedWars' Season 9 tree — since removed, which is stated in the reference — published prerequisites like 'Diamond Era + Destruction I' and 'Emerald Era + Magic I': a spine tier AND the previous step of the same branch. Deepwoken writes a talent's prerequisites as '[15 Fortitude OR 15 Willpower, 30 intelligence, Other]'. A single-parent model cannot express either, and a node with a disjunctive prerequisite belongs under more than one branch.

rules.rule: Re-render the inventory after an upgrade purchase, because a node can change items already held.
rules.why: BedWars' Iron Arrows upgrade 'unlocks iron arrows and upgrades any arrows already in the inventory', and Charging Gloops does the same. The purchase happens in one screen and the mutation lands in another. BOTH ROWS ARE DATED REMOVED April 5, 2024 in the Team Upgrades table's own 'Date Of Removal' column, and nothing else read for this file shows the behaviour, so the rule rests entirely on a system BedWars no longer runs. The mechanism is worth copying; the evidence for it is historical, which this reason did not say until 2026-09-20.

rules.rule: Accept that a node's payload may be rows in a DIFFERENT screen, and put the locked state there.
rules.why: BedWars' Armory upgrade 'unlocks several combat items inside of the Item Shop'. The tree records that the node is bought; the shop is where the items stop being locked. A tree that tries to show the items itself duplicates the shop. The Armory row is dated removed June 23, 2023, and the only other example read here — a Brewing Stand row unlocking 5 Unique Potions in the Item Shop — is inside the Season 9 table the page files under 'Removed'. Both sources for this rule are historical.

rules.rule: A fixed level ladder needs a reached/not-reached state, not an affordability state — and it should say the player does not choose.
rules.why: TDS tower evolution: 'the player does not get to pick which upgrades they unlock as each one has a determined level it is unlocked on', the progress shows as an orange bar on the inventory tile, and for an unevolved tower 'the only level that actually matters is the last one'. That bar is progress toward ONE gate, and drawing its intermediate stops as purchasable nodes would be a lie.

rules.rule: Reach the crafting or upgrade screen from a place or a person when the game has a world to put it in.
rules.why: BedWars' team upgrades are bought by 'interacting with Fulco, who can be found in each team's base'; Fisch's crafting altar is inside the Ancient Archives; Islands' workbench is a block on the player's island that is spawned with the island. A world that already has a location for the screen and also floats a button for it has two entry points to keep in sync.

rules.rule: Make crafting output a placement token rather than the finished object when the thing is placed in the world.
rules.why: In 99 Nights in the Forest the bench produces a Crafting Blueprint into the inventory, and placement is a separate step with its own controls — the game's own tips include 'Press R to rotate structures before you place them.' Crafting and placing are two screens' worth of state and one of them is the world.

rules.rule: Let an upgrade ladder introduce a new currency at the top rather than only scaling the old one.
rules.why: 99 Nights prices bench tiers 1-3 in Wood and Scrap, tier 4 adds Cultist Gems, tier 5 adds Gem of the Forest. The price row grows a slot partway up, which is a clearer statement that the top is a different kind of goal than a larger number in the same slot.

rules.rule: Keep the node graph as data, so the tree can be re-balanced by someone who cannot script.
rules.why: The developer of a 750-ability tree said the hard part was 'making it able to be easily customizable and allowing the developers to create skill trees with virtually no programming knowledge'. A tree whose graph is hand-placed is a tree nobody re-balances. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS RULE WAS DELETED ON 2026-09-20. It said to expect to draw the edges with something other than a Frame, on the strength of the same author's 'isn’t a GUI but bricks using beams to connect them'. Post 15 of that same topic, two years later, is that author saying he 'ended up making a completely 2D version of this skill tree'. A ScreenGui still has no line primitive, but nothing read here settles what to draw an edge with, and the only developer who answered the question answered it twice and differently.

limits: WHAT A LOCKED NODE LOOKS LIKE IS THE THINNEST PART OF THIS FILE AND SHOULD BE FIXED BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED FOR ONE. Nothing read here describes the rendering of an unaffordable recipe or an unreached node — not a dim, not a desaturation, not a padlock, not an outline, not a strike-through on a missing ingredient. The two closest statements are BedWars' Forge showing a COUNT of currently-available upgrades, which says how many and not which, and one DevForum author's description of his own unreleased screen in which 'the craft button lights up' once the ingredients are held. That second one is intent, not a shipped rendering, and it is quoted as such. Everything this file says about locked states is about their SEMANTICS — unreached, unaffordable, mode-excluded, blueprint-missing, capped-out — and nothing about their pixels.

No numeric measurement of any kind was found: no grid column count, cell size, stroke weight, corner radius, padding or font size appears in any source read here. Nothing in this file should be used as a measurement. The single exception is a reviewer asking for '2-3 pixels' more gap between a header bar and the content sheet below it, which is one person's eye on one screenshot.

Fandom serves article HTML behind Cloudflare, so all eight wikis were read through api.php as wikitext. That is the same content, but it means the SCREENSHOTS those pages embed were named and not seen. Every claim in the eleven wiki-backed references is one the page states in prose or in a table, never one inferred from an image nobody looked at — the five DevForum references are a different case and the adversarial limit below names the two of their claims that still rest on an unseen screenshot. Where a page's structure is the wiki's own, that is NOT recorded as the game's interface: the tabbed layout of Fisch's rod list, the colour-coded rows of BedWars' Season 9 table, the rowspan that groups a BedWars upgrade's tier rows under one icon, and the star-and-skull glyphs in the Forge table's Level column. The last of those was recorded as the game's rendering until 2026-09-20 and is the reason this limit now lists instances rather than gesturing at a category.

MORE OF THIS FILE IS HISTORICAL THAN THE FIRST TWO PASSES ADMITTED. BedWars' Forge page is flagged as removed (17 November 2023), which was always recorded here. What was not: the Team Upgrades page's MAIN table has its own 'Date Of Removal' column, and five of its eleven upgrade entries are dated — Iron Arrows, Charging Gloops and Healing Fountain on April 5, 2024, the three Mining tiers on April 28, 2023, and Armory on June 23, 2023. Three rules in this file rest wholly or mostly on those dated rows — re-rendering the inventory after an upgrade purchase, a node whose payload is rows in another screen, and tiered and untiered nodes in one list — and each now says so in its own reason. Add the Season 9 prerequisite table, also filed under Removed, and the Deepwoken page, which carries an Outdated banner and states it has documented 71 of about 200 talent trees. Their SHAPES are what is recorded; no price, tier or talent from any of them should be treated as current.

Five of the sixteen references are DevForum threads about unreleased hobby projects, not shipped games. Their value is the critique and the named construction traps — the single craft button bound to every row, the TextScaled ingredient line, the unlabelled regions — not evidence that anybody shipped them. They are marked as feedback threads in their source fields, and the eight wiki-backed shipped games carry the structural claims.

Nothing read here covers a GRID-SHAPED crafting surface — the Minecraft-style arrangement where the positions of the ingredients matter. The 2024 DevForum thread has 'crafting spaces' the ingredients ghost into, but the thread never says whether their arrangement is significant, and none of the shipped games read here uses one; all five material-recipe games express a recipe as an unordered list of counts. A request for a shaped-recipe grid is unbacked.

Nothing read here covers a multi-recipe queue. Bee Swarm's Blender is the only timed queue in the file and it is explicitly one recipe deep; the other material-recipe crafting screens read here state no timer at all. A request for a crafting queue with several different items pending, each with its own timer, has no source behind it.

Craft-all was searched for and NOT FOUND as a named control in any shipped source. The closest is Bee Swarm's quantity selector plus a Confirm, and that is a quantity, not a 'craft everything I can afford'. Nothing here says what a craft-all does about partial affordability, about per-run caps, or about which recipe it picks.

Eight shipped games is a reasonable sample but a skewed one: five of them are survival or sandbox games whose recipes consume materials, and three are upgrade trees whose only ingredient is a currency or a point. Nothing here is backed by a cooking, alchemy, fusion or gacha-merge screen, and those differ most in the place this file is already weakest — how an unavailable option is drawn.

THREE HOSTILE PASSES HAVE READ THIS FILE AND EACH FOUND FINER ERRORS THAN THE ONE BEFORE. That is what converging looks like, and it is also what a process looks like just before somebody declares victory, so the whole history is recorded here rather than only its last line.

PASS ONE re-fetched every cited source and corrected fourteen statements — nine observations across six references, one reference's source line and four rule reasons — in four kinds. (1) A COUNT ADVERTISED AS COUNTED, AND WRONG: TDS has seventeen skills, not sixteen, and its level caps include a 10 the enumerated set omitted; Fisch's rod recipes use six Driftwood variants, not seven; the crafting-menu DevForum thread carries six author screenshots, not eight revisions. (2) AGREEMENT RESOLD AS INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: the two reviewers said to have asked for search independently were one stated reason and one reply beginning 'Adding on to the person above me', and the reading-order claim had the same shape. (3) MISATTRIBUTION BETWEEN A NODE AND ITS PREREQUISITE: the '29 shots required' ladder is Precision's, not Fight Dirty's. (4) A WIKI TABLE READ AS A GAME SCREEN: BedWars' icon 'spanning' its tier rows was the table's rowspan.

THAT PASS'S ARITHMETIC CANNOT BE CHECKED BY YOU, AND THIS ENTRY USED TO PRESENT IT AS FACT. The file is untracked and has no earlier version in the repository, so 'fourteen statements', 'nothing was deleted outright' and 'no reference lost an observation' are the editing session's own report on itself. The four categories are checkable against the current text and they hold; the counts are a self-report and are now labelled as one.

PASS TWO read the repaired file and found nine more items in it, all graded minor — part of sixty-four across the seven files it re-read. Its lesson was structural: a repair pass can fix a claim in one place and leave the same wording in another, and can leave a summary describing a file that no longer exists.

PASS THREE, this one, worked that list and is the last repair round. It changed thirty-two fields in this file — twenty-nine claim-bearing strings plus three of these limits entries — and that number is checkable by diffing this file against its state before 2026-09-20 if anyone keeps a copy, which is more than can be said for pass one's. FIVE CLAIMS WERE DELETED OUTRIGHT: (i) that BedWars' Forge draws a node's level as repeated star glyphs — that is the wiki table's Level column, the page's own prose numbers the levels 'Lvl 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Titan', and it is the same error class pass one had just fixed one reference earlier; (ii) that bold was how a DevForum thread settled a requirements heading — the thread never says, the outcome is an unseen screenshot, and the last reply to address it prefers the line; (iii) that Islands' category row is part of the list rather than a control above it, which no page states; (iv) that the category row 'arrives with the list length', which was read off two pages that say nothing about categories at all; and (v) the half of a rule that said to expect to draw tree edges with something other than a Frame, because post 15 of the cited topic is its own author saying he 'ended up making a completely 2D version of this skill tree'. THE REST WERE NARROWED: five quotations that had been silently typo-corrected are now quoted as posted, in the six places they appear; Fisch's 'each of the three axes can be zero' is two of three, because no recipe on that page has an empty material list; Islands' tier 3 says recipes 'can be sorted' where tier 4 says 'are sorted', and both verbs are now given; the BedWars removal dates landed in one source line, three observations and three rule reasons; the skill-tree author's reversal landed in one observation and one rule; two claims about the 2024 thread's outcome now say they are reported rather than seen; and one source line that said 'Cool Creations' now says what the category lookup this file's provenance describes actually returns, 'Creations Feedback'.

WHAT IS STILL UNSETTLED, BY NAME, BECAUSE A FILE THAT CLAIMS TO BE CLEAN IS THE KIND OF CLAIM THIS LIBRARY EXISTS TO DISTRUST. (a) THE FISCH PAGE DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ABOUT HOW MANY RODS IT LISTS: its prose says 'Currently, there are 15 rods that can be crafted' and nineteen rod tabs are present. No claim here states a number, and the 'every recipe carries at least one ingredient' check above was run over all nineteen, but neither figure should be quoted from this file. (b) TWO CLAIMS ABOUT THE 2024 CRAFTING-MENU THREAD REPORT AN OUTCOME NOBODY HERE SAW: that the author reordered to ingredients-then-output, and that he rebuilt the ingredient line as a grid. The advice is quoted and real and the author says in text that he took it; the result is in screenshots this file cannot look at, and both rows now say so. The same defect is what killed the bold-heading claim, and these two survived only because the author stated his intent in text before posting the picture. (c) WHETHER ISLANDS' LOWER WORKBENCH TIERS HAVE CATEGORY FILTERS is unknown — the wiki is silent, and this file read that silence as absence once already. (d) WHAT AN UNAFFORDABLE RECIPE LOOKS LIKE is still unanswered by anything read here, as the first limit has said from the start; three hostile passes have not turned up a single source that draws one.
